summary.text: The Cool Flames Investigation aims to examine droplet combustion of n-dodecane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures, including helium dilution and the relation between droplet size, pressure and extinction, using the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus in the Combustion Integrated Rack.

fuels.text: n-dodecane, farnesane, and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane.

geometry.text: Fuel droplets suspended between hypodermic needles or tethered using silicon-carbide fibers.

oxygen.text: Fuels diluted with molecular oxygen, atomic nitrogen, and helium; no concentrations stated.

pressure.text: Pressures from 0.25 atm to 5 atm are stated as an objective. The approach states a gas mixture delivered at 0.25 to 0.5 atm.

measurements.text: Droplet size by black-and-white camera, OH* radical emissions and flame size by UV camera, and flame radiation by narrow-band and wide-band radiometers.

hardware.text: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).

claims.text: The investigation aims to examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm.
The investigation aims to analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior.
The investigation aims to investigate the relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction.

The investigation hypothesizes that combustion of liquid hydrocarbon fuels in microgravity can provide insights into low-temperature chemical kinetics, revealing critical parameters like droplet extinction diameters and flame dynamics that are not observable on Earth.

limitations.text: The metadata gives different pressure ranges and no measured result. The objectives state 0.25 atm to 5 atm. The approach states 0.25 to 0.5 atm.
This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: Analyzed-data summary files for CFI dodecane flights listed in the PSI file inventory; the approach states droplet size and flame size were measured by camera.

evidence.excerpt: Examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm.
Analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool flame behavior.
Investigate the relationship between droplet size, pressure, and flame extinction
A UV camera was used for capturing the OH* radical emissions and flame size.
Fuels observed include n-dodecane, farnesane, and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane.
The Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) contains the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) which facilitates the controlled combustion of fuel droplets.
A system of gas bottles and fuel syringes delivers the desired gas mixture to the combustion chamber ranging from 0.25 to 0.5 atm.
Flames were observed with a black-and-white camera for droplet size measurements.
Droplets of fuel are dispensed and suspended between hypodermic needles or tethered using silicon-carbide fibers.
Fuels diluted with molecular oxygen, atomic nitrogen, and helium to study the influence on flame extinction and dynamics.
Narrow-band and wide-band radiometers for analyzed flame radiation.
